findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify BLOCK stickiness for the agentic engine: extend verdict_reuse (keyed on engine + material fingerprint + review code SHA) to agentic BLOCKs so an unchanged plan replays its stored agentic BLOCK, with `--force` the only explicit override.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:542-554: idempotent_reuse and verdict_reuse fire only when engine == "pipeline"
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:624-638: _apply_review_floors (remediation/drift floors) runs only under the pipeline engine
ADR 0123 §3: 'The agentic engine has no verify or decide pass' — the single agent assigns severity itself, so one re-roll is enough to flip a `blocker` to `major`
Plan 'No bypass' only requires 'a review', which a re-roll satisfies
findings.finding: Under the agentic engine the plan skips the pipeline's safeguards against re-rolling the same plan, so a stochastic single agent can be re-run on an unchanged plan until it returns zero `blocker`s. In the pipeline, BLOCK verdict reuse (bug 7e77) replays the stored BLOCK when material fingerprint and code SHA are unchanged. The remediation and drift floors also keep prior blockers from silently disappearing. The implementation gates all of these on `engine == "pipeline"`, and the plan names no agentic equivalent. The 'Same surfaces' invariant lists de-dup and GATE_CONGESTED but not BLOCK reuse.
findings.location: Invariants → 'No bypass' / 'Same surfaces'; Approach step 4 (Verdict adapter)
scenarios: An agentic run BLOCKs on one `blocker`. Without changing the plan, the author re-runs `review-plan`. The agent now labels the same defect `major`, and a PASS attestation is signed.
An MCP client polls review_plan_start repeatedly on an unchanged ticket and each call pays for a fresh agent run instead of getting the stored BLOCK.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the Approach and Invariants: 'An agentic BLOCK is reused, like a pipeline BLOCK, when the material fingerprint and review code SHA are unchanged and the prior sidecar's coverage.engine equals the current engine. Only --force/--retry bypass this.' Change the reuse.verdict_reuse engine check from `!= "pipeline"` to `!= current engine` and add an AC test that a second agentic run on an unchanged BLOCKed plan makes zero LLM calls and returns BLOCK.

evidence: Plan: "Only a clean, completed run with zero `blocker` findings is a PASS."
The plan defines no minimum review evidence (tool reads, criteria considered) before an agentic PASS can be certified.
findings.finding: Under the agentic engine, PASS only requires that the run 'finish cleanly with schema-valid output' and contain zero `blocker` findings. A degenerate run that makes no tool calls, reads no code and returns `{"findings": []}` meets that and mints a certified attestation. The pipeline has structural coverage: every routed criterion chunk must return, and missing coverage resolves INDETERMINATE. The agentic engine has nothing comparable. Its fail-closed list covers errors, limits, truncation, refusal and invalid output, but not an empty or trivial review that is schema-valid.
findings.location: Invariants — 'Fail closed' ("Only a clean, completed run with zero `blocker` findings is a PASS"); Approach step 3

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a 'Failure-disposition contract:' clause mapping each agentic failure class to retryable (exit-11/WAIT_AND_RETRY) or permanent (NEEDS_INVESTIGATION), and stating that when the Anthropic fallback fails the chain preserves the primary's retryable disposition (including on mid-loop failover); pin with a test.
evidence: 'resolves INDETERMINATE through the same `resolution_class` path a failed pipeline pass uses' — no retryable-vs-permanent split per class
Step 3: 'Bedrock-first with fallback still applies' — no fallback-failure winner
Step 2: 'with their Anthropic fallbacks, to Opus 5.5 ...' — the fallback arm is altered
findings.finding: The failure-disposition contract is incomplete on two arms. (1) The agentic engine folds every failure into INDETERMINATE but never says which classes stay retryable/transient and which are permanent. Retryable classes would be a provider throttle, a 5xx or a timeout, surfacing as exit-11 / WAIT_AND_RETRY. Permanent classes would be schema-invalid output, a refusal or content_filter, or exhausted limits, surfacing as NEEDS_INVESTIGATION. (2) The plan keeps the 'Bedrock-first with fallback' chain for the long agentic run and moves the Anthropic fallbacks to new 5.5 ids. It doesn't state which disposition wins when the fallback itself fails, or what happens on a mid-loop failover. A wrong or unavailable 5.5 fallback id (non-retryable 400 or auth error) could mask a retryable Bedrock 429 — the 1c0d root cause.
findings.location: Invariants (Fail closed) / Approach steps 2–3
scenarios: A Bedrock 429 mid-run fails over to Anthropic, whose 5.5 id or auth fails, and the caller sees a permanent failure instead of WAIT_AND_RETRY
Timeout and schema-invalid output both report the same disposition, so automation retries a deterministic failure forever
findings.suggested_fix: Contract: provider throttle, 5xx and timeout → INDETERMINATE, retryable (exit-11/WAIT_AND_RETRY); refusal, content_filter, schema-invalid output, max_tokens truncation and step/iteration exhaustion → INDETERMINATE, permanent (NEEDS_INVESTIGATION); if the Bedrock leg is retryable and the Anthropic fallback fails non-retryably, surface the Bedrock leg's retryable disposition (via `classify_llm_failure` / `should_fall_back`).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the agent's read-only view is pinned to the reviewed ref in every harness shape (e.g. reads resolved from git objects at the pinned SHA, not the working tree), and add a test that a stale workspace is not what the agent reads.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the stakeholder and the concrete problem a single-agent engine solves, and state what harness result (e.g. an agreement or recall target) would validate it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make 'No bypass' enforceable: specify that only an attestation from the configured `[verify] plan_review_engine` is certifying (claim/close gates compare `manifest_engine` to the configured engine), or that a per-call engine override different from the configured one runs unsigned (comparison only).
evidence: Plan: 'Switching engines can't turn a BLOCK into a PASS without a review: the attestation binds the plan material and the engine.'
Plan: 'A non-blocking agentic PASS mints the same plan-review attestation, accepted identically by the claim and close gates'
docs/adr/0123 §1: 'Precedence: an explicit `engine` argument to `review_plan` (which the CLI `--engine` flag, the MCP tools and the comparison harness pass) over the config key'
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:229-232: a pipeline run returns None (no reuse) when the prior BLOCK sidecar's engine is not pipeline
src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest_gate.py:247-263: engine is only reported on status, not checked against the configured engine
ADR 0123 Consequences: 'a project can audit or restrict engines later' — so restriction is deferred, not designed
findings.finding: The 'No bypass' invariant's stated mechanism ('the attestation binds the plan material and the engine') does not stop engine-shopping. The engine is only recorded on the attestation. The claim and close gates accept either engine's attestation 'identically', and the engine can be chosen per call: the precedence the ADR records puts an explicit `engine` argument, i.e. the CLI `--engine` flag or the MCP tools, above `[verify] plan_review_engine`. An author whose plan the configured engine BLOCKs can re-run with the other engine and get a signed PASS that the claim gate accepts. reuse.verdict_reuse explicitly refuses to carry blockers across engines, so the prior BLOCK has no effect.
findings.location: Invariants → 'No bypass'; Invariants → 'Same certification'; Approach step 1 (engine switch precedence)
scenarios: A project configures `pipeline`. Its 4-pass review BLOCKs a plan. The author runs `rebar review-plan <id> --engine agentic`, the single agent finds no `blocker`, a PASS attestation is signed, and `claim` succeeds without the configured reviewer ever passing the plan.
The reverse also works: a project on `agentic` falls back to `--engine pipeline` to dodge an agentic blocker.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Invariants and the ADR, state that the claim/close gates (attest_gate.claim_gate_check / compute_validity) treat an attestation whose recorded engine differs from the currently configured `[verify] plan_review_engine` as non-certifying, with a distinct reason such as `wrong-engine`. Alternatively, `review_plan` forces `sign=False` when an explicit `engine` argument differs from the configured key. Add an AC test: a pipeline BLOCK followed by `--engine agentic` PASS does not let `claim` through.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In the ADR, address ADR 0075's single-pass retirement: explain why a single-agent plan-review PASS may carry the same certification as the 4-pass kernel, and cite the bakeoff or comparison evidence on blocker recall that supports it.
evidence: docs/adr/0075-retire-single-pass-code-review.md: 'It had NO Pass-2 verifier, NO deterministic Pass-3 decision ... Keeping both would be a half-migration: two code-review code paths, one of which silently lacks verification/decision rigor.'
Plan: 'A non-blocking agentic PASS mints the same plan-review attestation, accepted identically by the claim and close gates'

ADR 0123 Consequences admits only the false-positive side: 'The agentic engine's findings have no verify pass behind them, so its false-positive rate is a property of the prompt and model alone'. The certification risk is false negatives (a missed blocker on PASS), and neither the plan nor the ADR addresses it.
Absence: the plan names the operator's ~/plan-review-bakeoff prompt as its source but cites no bakeoff results to justify the new engine.
findings.finding: The plan adds a single-agent review engine that mints the same certifying attestation as the 4-pass kernel, but never addresses rebar's own earlier decision against single-pass review. ADR 0075 retired the single-pass code-review route because it had 'NO Pass-2 verifier, NO deterministic Pass-3 decision', and said keeping both routes would mean one 'silently lacks verification/decision rigor'. The plan does not explain why plan review differs, and it cites no bakeoff or eval evidence that the single agent's blocker recall matches the pipeline's.
findings.location: Goal 1 / Approach §3 (Agentic engine) / Invariants 'Same certification'
scenarios: A project switches to `agentic`. A plan the pipeline would BLOCK gets PASS with a valid attestation because no verify/decide pass catches the miss. That is the 'silently lacks rigor' outcome ADR 0075 rejected.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Point the comparison harness and its recorded AC run at the ADR 0109 plan-replay whole-plan labels corpus instead of the `evals/` criterion fragments, which the Layer-1 floor blocks before either engine runs.

docs/adr/0109-plan-review-replay-harness.md: the plan_replay harness and its persisted REVIEW_RESULT/labels corpus already exist for whole-plan replay.
findings.finding: The comparison harness is told to run on `evals/`, but that corpus cannot discriminate between the engines. The repo's engine_comparison.py says those cases are single-criterion fragments the Layer-1 floor blocks before either engine runs, so both engines trivially agree. The established whole-plan corpus is the ADR 0109 plan-replay labels corpus, and the plan does not name it.

scenarios: The AC's recorded corpus run reports ~100% verdict agreement because every case floor-blocks with zero LLM calls. The comparison looks like it passes while measuring nothing about either engine.
findings.suggested_fix: Change Approach §5 to: 'Run it over the whole-plan rows of the plan-review replay labels corpus (`rebar.llm.evals.plan_replay`, ADR 0109)', and change the AC to 'One run over the replay labels corpus is recorded in a ticket comment.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Have the comparison harness report each engine's identical-run reproduction floor (verdict flip rate and finding Jaccard) next to cross-engine agreement, per ADR 0109's noise-band rule, or record in the ADR why that rule does not apply.
evidence: docs/adr/0109 §5: 'A change is judged improving/regressing only when it moves outside its own tier's band' — Tier 2 metric is 'finding-set Jaccard ... + candidate-vs-stored verdict flip matrix' against 'an identical-candidate reproduction run'.
Plan: 'report verdict agreement and the finding overlap' — no noise floor or reproduction run is mentioned.
findings.finding: The comparison harness reports raw verdict agreement and finding overlap without the noise-band rule ADR 0109 sets for exactly these metrics. That rule requires an identical-candidate reproduction run, and a change counts as signal only outside that run's flip-rate/Jaccard floor. Without each engine's own self-agreement floor, cross-engine disagreement cannot be told apart from model nondeterminism. The plan does not say whether it builds on or departs from this established method.
findings.location: Approach §5 (Comparison harness) / AC 'reports verdict agreement and finding overlap'
scenarios: The pipeline flips PASS↔BLOCK on, say, 15% of identical re-runs by itself. A 15% cross-engine disagreement then gets read as an engine difference when it is noise.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define each severity (blocker/major/minor/trivial) with entry criteria in the ADR, and require the new prompt to state those definitions next to the findings output schema.

scenarios: The model marks a real ship-stopping gap as `major`, the plan PASSes and gets an attestation the claim gate accepts

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the agent's output field set (id, description, severity, evidence, criteria, location, …) and a field-by-field mapping to sidecar finding keys, including defaults for pipeline-only fields (decision, priority, validity, impact) and the severity mapping.

Pipeline severity also uses a different vocabulary (`critical`) from the agentic one. So the claim 'downstream readers need no change' is unbacked.

A reader that sorts by `priority` or filters on pipeline severity values drops or mis-ranks agentic findings

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the failure-class field and its closed value set, and give the exact ResolutionClass value set for each failure kind (error, timeout, tool-step/iteration limit, max_tokens, refusal/content_filter, invalid output).

findings.suggested_fix: Extend Approach step 2 and AC 2 to name every site the derivation finds, at minimum: `config.DEFAULT_MODEL`, `config.VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `model_classes.TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL`, `review_kernel/verify.MODEL_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, `capabilities._MODEL_CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` / `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` / `_SAMPLING_ACCEPTING_MODEL_IDS`, `plan_review/registry.chunk_by_facet`'s `model=` default, and `evals/fixture_emit._MODEL`. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile 2886's 'identical results' floor criterion with 75af's engine stamp on floor verdicts by naming exactly which fields must match (verdict, blocking, advisory) and allowing coverage.engine to differ.

75af Testing: "Floor verdicts carry `coverage.engine` under agentic"

findings.finding: 75af stamps `coverage.engine = engine` on every non-pipeline verdict, including floor verdicts. A floor-blocked plan reviewed under "agentic" therefore returns a verdict and sidecar that differ from the pipeline result, because pipeline coverage has no `engine` key. That contradicts 2886's checked criterion and approach, which require identical, byte-identical results under both values for floor-blocked and not-claimable reviews.
findings.location: child 75af-1212-aa22-463f
scenarios: 2886's identical-results test compares whole verdicts under both engines and now fails, or was weakened without saying so.
A sidecar consumer that compares floor results across engines sees a difference.
findings.suggested_fix: Amend 2886's AC2 to say 'identical verdict, blocking and advisory (coverage.engine aside)', and have 75af's floor test assert equality on those fields.

findings.finding: 526b's deploy precondition only checks the deployed image SHA (`/var/lib/rebar/mcp-deployed-sha`). Its siblings 6b02 and 0bc1 show that the production MCP server reads its config, rebar.toml with the model classes, from the separate code workspace REBAR_ROOT=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code, and that this workspace can lag the image. 526b neither lists 6b02 or 0bc1 as preconditions nor checks the workspace HEAD. scenarios: The image SHA contains 4240326388e but the mcp-code workspace is stale. Production runs then resolve 4.x model classes, or workspace-sourced code without the engine, yet still meet the completion rule.
